label: PF Backlog 4
title: WG-O4: Merge-driver coverage for id-blocks.json (max-merge) + children[] regenerated
body: Part of EPIC BI-PF-0360. Source: docs/WORKER-SCHEDULER-OPERATIONS.md.

brief.problem: config/id-blocks.json and epic children[] conflict on parallel merges.
brief.what_adds: id-blocks.json attached to the pf-derived max-merge driver; epic.children[] materialized-but-regenerated (derived).
brief.why: Removes today's most common backlog merge conflicts.

objective: Extend the derived merge driver to id-blocks and children.
acceptance_criteria: .gitattributes attaches config/id-blocks.json to the pf-derived max-merge driver.
epic.children[] is regenerated on merge (derived), not text-merged, but stays materialized for readers.
A merge of two divergent backlogs yields no conflict in id-blocks/children.
approach: Attach id-blocks to the existing max-merge; regenerate children[] during merge.
verification: synthetic two-side merge keeps max reserved_up_to + union sessions; children regenerated.

analysis.implementation_strategy: Add a max-merge merge-driver script for config/id-blocks.json (e.g., tools/merge_id_blocks.py) wired via .gitattributes; script parses both sides, takes max per id-block key, and regenerates children[] arrays from the merged id list. Reuse core/backlog.py id parsing if available; add tests in core/nfr_coverage.py style.
dependency_findings: RELATED BI-PF-1327 (canonical repo/worktree) — concurrent branches make merge-drivers important but not strictly blocking.
REQUIRES git >= 2.38 for merge-driver support on worker machines (assumption).
conflict_findings: config/id-blocks.json may be concurrently edited by workers in BI-PF-1327 sessions; merge-driver mitigates rather than conflicts.
No other backlog item claims .gitattributes or id-blocks merge logic.
duplication_findings: No existing merge-driver or id-blocks JSON merge logic found in candidate components.
core/nfr_coverage.py is a coverage validator, not a merger — only tangentially reusable for validation of regenerated children.
analysis.rationale: Workers branching in parallel will constantly conflict on id-blocks.json; a max-merge driver plus regenerated children[] removes the main source of merge pain in the WG epic.
assumptions: id-blocks.json is flat {key: block} with numeric ids and children[] derived from keys.
File lives at config/id-blocks.json in canonical repo.
risks: Merge driver correctness on malformed JSON during conflict states.
children[] regeneration could diverge from existing API validation (core/nfr_coverage.py).
Local git config (.gitattributes wiring) may be missed by existing workers.
missing_info: Exact schema of id-blocks.json (keys, children[] derivation rule) not verified by human.
Whether driver must be registered in repo .gitattributes vs per-worker git config.
Conflict-resolution policy for overlapping id reservations (max of ranges).

context_review.reason: Component and file exist; implementation is self-contained but schema details must be confirmed.

api_impact.reason: retrofit assessment (ADR-0007): no external API consumer recorded; treated as internal until an API surface is required (then set needs_api=true with routes)
